items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn’t actually meet him . . . I’m not sure if I ever . . . if I met him it was peripherally

ctx.x: I was aware of him on records. There were a lot more d.j.’s playing jazz then than there are now. Every town you would be in, there would be at least one radio station. That’s something we all miss, but I haven’t thought of it ’til this minute. You would pick up on a lot of new people and new stuff, because you’d hear it on the radio. A guy like Dave Garroway, he was insatiable for wanting to hear new people and

playing it. So I had a lot of records of Phineas. I didn’t actually meet him . . . I’m not sure if I ever . . . if I met him it was peripherally, like “hello,” but I had a lot of his records. I remember a period when . . . Do you remember a name, John Mehegan?
